'Our cycling is a form of resistance': Gaza Sunbirds co-founder Karim Ali
items.description: A Palestinian charity says its daily work to provide food for Gazans by bicycle delivery is a form of resistance. The Gaza Sunbirds are a team of people, often athletes, who are dedicated to bringing food to those who need it most. items.title: Trump says U.S. and Iran nearing a peace deal. And, Pope Leo weighs in on AI's rise
items.description: President Trump says that a deal with Iran to end the war is largely negotiated. And, Pope Leo XIV weighed in today on the rise of AI during his first encyclical.

items.title: Trump’s war loop: Escalate, retreat, repeat
items.description: Stuck in a quagmire of a war, Trump chafes at negative coverage while Iran digs its heels in.

items.title: Amid Mounting Tensions Between Kyiv And Minsk, Belarus Opposition Leader Tsikhanouskaya Visits Ukraine
items.description: Svyatlana Tsikhanouskaya arrived in Kyiv, in the exiled Belarusian opposition leader’s first trip to Ukraine more than four years into the all-out Russian invasion.

items.title: Kyiv attacks: The complex logistics network behind Russia's war machine
items.description: The Ukrainian capital endured a barrage of strikes over the weekend, including ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and long-range drones. These increasingly frequent hybrid operations reveal the intensification of Russian drone and missile production.

items.title: Ex-hostage Maxim Herkin publishes book featuring a diary he secretly wrote in captivity
items.description: 'Coming to Light' recounts Herkin's experiences during his 2 years in the clutches of Hamas, including his success concealing the fact he was an IDF officer The post Ex-hostage Maxim Herkin publishes book featuring a diary he secretly wrote in captivity appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: Rosenberg: Luhansk strike sparks Russian accusations and vow to retaliate
items.description: Eighteen people were killed and 42 others injured in the strike on the town in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine.

items.title: Serbia: Police clash with protesters urging early elections
items.description: Officers fired teargas and stun grenades as tens of thousands rallied against President Aleksandar Vucic's government. The demonstration went ahead despite the state rail operator canceling trains to and from Belgrade.

items.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Russian Oil Depot
items.description: Two people were wounded in an attack on Russia's fifth largest oil export hub in Novorossiysk, the local mayor said.
